title: service-dependency-isolation-and-runtime-feature-gating-standards-2026
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood's standards for service dependency isolation and runtime feature-gating. The goal is to provide a predictable, auditable, and recoverable mechanism for enabling/disabling features and for isolating service dependencies (datastores, external APIs, model variants, compute pools) so that rollouts, incident mitigations, and capacity-driven fallbacks happen safely and consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Why this matters:
- Uncontrolled feature flags or coarse dependency coupling lead to cross-customer incidents and unpredictable unit costs.
- Runtime gating must interact with routing, model fallback, and quota policies in a coherent way.
- Isolation and gating enable rapid safe rollouts (canary/gradual), predictable degradation during capacity shortages, and fast incident mitigation.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood services and runtime components that influence request routing or resource selection: gateway, routing service, model router, autoscaler, and per-tenant policy agents.
- Covers feature flags, dependency-level circuit breakers, resource pool segregation, and fallback routing rules.
- Excludes UI-only client-side experiment flags (those are handled in product experiment tooling).

Design Principles:
1) Declarative policy over ad-hoc code: all gating decisions that affect live routing or resource selection must be expressed as declarative policy artifacts stored in the config store and versioned.
2) Fast, auditable rollbacks: changes must be reversible without a code deploy. Every policy change must be tied to an auditable change record (change-id).
3) Safety-first defaults: new gates default to off for critical-path changes, and to fail-closed for read/write dependency faults.
4) Observability-driven: gating must emit structured telemetry (decision reasons, policy ids, sampling id) to link decisions to customer impact and SLOs.
5) Decoupled ownership: feature gating policy ownership is product + owning-service, while runtime enforcement is infra/serving runtime.

Standards and Requirements:
- Policy Format: JSON or YAML, must include: id, service, owner, created_at, version, conditions, action, rollback_strategy, linked_change_id.
- Versioning: semantic versioning for policy artifacts (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Any MAJOR change (incompatible condition semantics) must go through an ADR and staged rollout.
- Storage: policies stored in the central config store (config.redwood.internal) with history. Local caches on nodes must honor TTLs and expose last-applied-version.
- Enforcement: runtime components must evaluate policy in-line before routing decisions. If evaluation fails, an enforcement default must be used (see Failover table).

Minimal Policy Schema (human readable):
| Field | Type | Description |
| ------ | ---- | ----------- |
| id | string | unique policy id (policy/<service>/<name>) |
| service | string | owning service name |
| owner | string | team or person |
| created_at | date | ISO8601 |
| version | string | semver |
| conditions | list | predicates (header, tenant, percent, time-window, capacity-threshold) |
| action | string | enable | disable | route-to-pool | fallback |
| target | string | pool, model-variant, external-endpoint |
| rollback_strategy | string | immediate | gradual | revert-to-version |
| linked_change_id | string | changelog / ticket id |

Example policy (JSON):
{
  "id": "policy/model-router/disable-variant-x-2026-02",
  "service": "model-router",
  "owner": "platform-models",
  "created_at": "2026-02-01T10:12:00Z",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "conditions": [
    {"type": "tenant", "value": "trial-*"},
    {"type": "percent_rollout", "value": 100}
  ],
  "action": "route-to-pool",
  "target": "variant-y",
  "rollback_strategy": "immediate",
  "linked_change_id": "CHG-3821"
}

Failover and Default Behavior Table:
| Failure Mode | Enforcement Default | Alerting |
|--------------|---------------------|---------|
| Policy evaluation timeout | Use last-known-good policy version | Error:policy:evaluation:timeout |
| Invalid policy syntax | Reject change, use previous version | Error:policy:invalid |
| Target pool missing | Route to configured-fallback pool or degrade-to-hosted | Warning:route:fallback |
| Authorization failure | Deny and emit audit event | Error:policy:auth |

Runtime Implementation Notes:
- Evaluation path must be O(1) or O(log N) per request; expensive predicates (heavy external lookups) are disallowed in hot-path. Use pre-computed tokens or cached context.
- Gate decisions must annotate traces with: policy.id, policy.version, decision (allow/deny/route), reason-code. Example trace tag: policy:policy/model-router/disable-variant-x-2026-02@1.0.0=route-to-pool(variant-y).
- Provide a runtime hook for manual emergency overrides with a higher-priority ephemeral policy. Ephemeral policies must be limited to 1 hour by default and require a change ticket recorded within 24h.

Deployment and Rollout Procedures (standardized):
1) Author policy artifact in config repo using the policy template.
2) Open a change request: include description, owners, SLO impact analysis, test plan.
3) Dry-run: deploy policy with action:dry-run for 1 hour against 1% traffic of target service (prefer staging tenants).
4) Observe: check impact on request success rate, p50/p95 latency, token cost delta. Minimum observation window: 30 minutes or 1000 requests, whichever is larger.
5) Gradual rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with at least 30 minutes at each step and automated health checks.
6) Automated abort: if any of the SLOs break (configured below), rollback immediately to previous policy version.

Health Checks and SLOs for Rollouts:
- Request success rate (service-level): must not degrade > 0.5 percentage points from baseline over 30 minutes.
- Latency: p95 must not increase > 15% relative to baseline.
- Cost: estimated per-token cost change must not exceed configured threshold for target pool and tenant class.
- Error budget: if error budget consumed > 60% in last 1h for that service, all non-critical rollouts are blocked.

Observability and Alerting:
- Telemetry keys: policy.id, policy.version, decision, decision_reason, target_pool, tenant_id, request_id. Each decision must emit a compact event to the decision-bus.
- Dashboards: maintain an "Active Policy Decisions" dashboard per service showing top policies by hit-rate, decision breakdown, and correlated SLO deltas.
- Alerts (examples):
  - alert:PolicyErrorRateHigh
    condition: policy_decision_errors > 0.5% over 5m
  - alert:PolicyRolloutAbort
    condition: automated_abort_triggered == true

Ownership and Governance:
- Authoring: product or owning-service authors policies. Policies must include an explicit owner (person or team).
- Reviewers: infra/security must be a reviewer for policies that change routing or model selection.
- Quarterly audit: infra performs a quarterly audit of all active policies and stale ephemeral overrides.

Migration and Backfill Plan for Existing Flags:
- Inventory: run a scan to list all existing ad-hoc flags and hard-coded fallbacks.
- Categorize: safety-critical, cost-control, customer-experience.
- Backfill: convert safety-critical first into policy artifacts; provide adapters at runtime to map legacy flag keys to policy ids.
- Deadline: legacy flags for routing must be removed within 6 months of policy-compliance cutoff.

Security and Compliance Considerations:
- Access control: writing and approving policies is RBAC-protected. Only authorized teams can create MAJOR version policies.
- Audit trail: every change to policy persists who changed what, prior content, and a changelist id.
- Data residency: policy evaluation may include tenant metadata; ensure any sensitive tenant attributes are redacted from telemetry if configured by the tenant (Private deployments).

Testing Guidance and Local Development:
- Use the policy-sim tool (open-source repo: infra/policy-sim) for unit testing policy logic locally. Sample command:
  ./policy-sim --policy ./examples/disable-variant.json --trace sample-requests.json
- Integration tests: use the canary harness to simulate traffic under different pool failures and assert fallback behavior (see infra/canary-playbook).

Emergency Playbook (incident mitigation):
1) Identify harmful policy decision in traces (search by policy.id).
2) Apply ephemeral override to block decision (CLI example):
  curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLI_TOKEN" \
    https://config.redwood.internal/policies/ephemeral \
    -d '{"target_policy":"policy/model-router/disable-variant-x-2026-02","action":"revert","ttl":3600}'
3) Notify stakeholders and open post-incident change to make ephemeral override permanent or to safely retire offending policy.

Open Questions / Future Work:
- Standardizing cross-service policy composition (how to evaluate combined model-router + gateway conditions atomically).
- Policy simulation at scale: integrating with perf-scheduler to predict cost delta under different rollout percentages.
- Tenant-specific sandboxing for Private deployments: whether tenant policies should be namespaced and evaluated independently from global platform policies.

Appendix: Example policy YAML (gradual disable with capacity condition):
---
id: policy/model-router/gradual-disable-variant-x
service: model-router
owner: platform-models
created_at: 2026-01-10T08:00:00Z
version: 1.1.0
conditions:
  - type: percent_rollout
    value: 25
  - type: capacity_threshold
    metric: gpu_free_pct
    operator: "<="
    value: 12
action: route-to-pool
target: variant-y
rollback_strategy: gradual
linked_change_id: CHG-3992
---

Appendix B: Suggested default labels for policy metadata:
- environment:[staging|prod|private]  (required)
- impact:[safety|cost|experience]  (required)
- tenant_class:[trial|standard|enterprise] (recommended)

Contacts and Owners:

- Policy authoring support: platform-models (owners: Priya Desai, Marco Chen)
